subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw allow the opt-in timeout to release the session lane while a prior same-session ContextEngine `maintain()` call is still running, thereby making re-entrant maintenance a supported plugin SDK behavior?
rationale: This is not only a local timeout implementation choice: it changes the execution semantics exposed to installed context-engine plugins, while the host can fence only its own writes and cannot cancel or serialize plugin-private effects.

options.title: Preserve serialized maintenance
options.body: Keep a timed-out maintenance run coalesced for its engine until it settles, or add a bounded engine-specific cancellation/ownership mechanism before another same-session `maintain()` begins.

options.title: Adopt re-entrant maintenance
options.body: Accept concurrent same-session `maintain()` as the SDK contract and require a compatibility strategy, explicit documentation, and focused upgrade proof for existing engines.

recommendation.title: Preserve serialized maintenance
recommendation.body: Keep a timed-out maintenance run coalesced for its engine until it settles, or add a bounded engine-specific cancellation/ownership mechanism before another same-session `maintain()` begins.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the proposed timeout, fencing, and explicit SDK-contract language and can clarify the intended implementation boundary; current-main feature ownership could not be independently established from the available read-only inspection channel.
